top_story: The regional picture has shifted from chronic crisis to sharper interstate escalation after a Strait of Hormuz attack triggered overnight US strikes on 28 June, followed by Iranian action against Bahrain and Kuwait that pushed Gulf states closer to the line of fire. By 29 June, this exchange was eroding a fragile interim US-Iran peace framework and raising the risk that shipping access, energy flows, and civilian security across the Gulf would be held hostage to coercive signaling. In Gaza, Israel’s 25 June bombing of beach tents sheltering displaced Palestinians reinforced the baseline reality that mass civilian vulnerability, siege, and hunger continue even as attention tilts toward the Gulf. The immediate analytical takeaway is that a widening US-Iran confrontation is not displacing existing wars so much as layering a more dangerous regional crisis on top of already devastated civilian landscapes.
